title: Pesto Béchamel Lasagne
changes_from_base: Meat-free and green: every layer is a basil pesto béchamel, finished with Parmesan and toasted pine nuts instead of ragù.
summary: A green lasagne layered with basil pesto béchamel and topped with Parmesan and toasted pine nuts.
equipment: salad spinner or clean tea towel

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, for blanching
ingredients.note: about 1 tbsp; most goes down the drain

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dried lasagne sheets (curly-edged if you can find them)

steps.title: White sauce
steps.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour for 1 min without colouring, then slowly whisk in the milk. Bring to the boil, add the pepper and nutmeg and whisk 1 min more until smooth and thick. Pour into a large bowl to cool for 20 min.

steps.title: Blanch the basil
steps.text: Bring 4 litres water to the boil with the blanching salt, drop in the basil for 5-10 s, then lift it out and spin or squeeze dry. Keep the water. Blanching sets the green colour so the pesto stays bright through baking.

steps.title: Pesto
steps.text: Blend the basil with the oil, pine nuts, garlic and salt until smooth, then stir it into the béchamel with the 55 g Parmesan and the lemon zest.

steps.title: Cook the sheets
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Bring the basil water back to the boil and cook the sheets until fully tender. Drain onto the oiled baking sheet, turn to coat and cut 2 in half.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread a ladle of sauce in the oiled dish and make 5 layers of sheets and sauce, with a half sheet filling the gap each time, ending with sauce. Scatter over the 30 g Parmesan and the remaining pine nuts.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover with oiled foil and bake 20 min, then uncover and bake 25-30 min until spotty brown and bubbling. Rest 20 min before cutting.

tips: Blanch the basil only a few seconds.
Cool the béchamel before adding the pesto.
Cook the sheets fully; the sauce is thick.
storage: Cool, cover and refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 3 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat covered in a 180 °C oven until piping hot (74 °C) in the centre.
